A Measured Datasheet for the iPhone 16 Pro Max Main Camera: Geometry, Resolution, Noise, and Color¶

Jon Knapp

Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Portland State University, Portland, OR, USA

EE 513 Intro to Image Processing, Project 1, November 2026

Repository: https://github.com/Jon-Knapp/EE513

Resume line: Engineered an open-source raw-sensor camera characterization toolkit in Python and OpenCV (slanted-edge MTF, photon-transfer noise modeling, color correction, geometric calibration) and published a measured datasheet for the iPhone 16 Pro Max, cross-checking my distortion model against Apple’s embedded lens correction to within 6 px.

Abstract—I characterized the main camera of an iPhone 16 Pro Max from its Bayer raw files, with an uncertainty and a method behind every figure. Calibration gives a focal length of 2901.8 ± 4.6 px (0.86 px RMS reprojection error). MTF50 is 0.453 ± 0.064 cycles per green-plane pixel at the center and 0.353 ± 0.050 at 82–84% of the way to the frame corners. Photon transfer at ISO 50 gives a conversion gain of 0.246 ± 0.021 DN/e⁻, a read noise of 6.9 ± 0.6 e⁻ and a dynamic range of 11.04 ± 0.06 stops. A color correction matrix reduces the mean CIEDE2000 error from 12.35 to 3.06 ± 0.04. Beyond the specification, the ultra-wide camera's raw distortion is under 1.6% out to 83% of the corner radius and matches Apple's own correction in the DNG to within 6 px, and a metal ruler that neither calibration saw tests both cameras.

Index Terms—Camera calibration, color correction, dynamic range, image sensor noise, lens distortion, modulation transfer function, photon transfer curve.

I. Introduction¶

This report measures what a spec sheet leaves out for the main (1×) rear camera of an iPhone 16 Pro Max; Section VIII repeats the geometry for the ultra-wide. All captures are Bayer DNGs, and the assignment's lens_id check passes on every series (Table I). The 48 MP quad-pixel sensor's 12 MP raw output is 2 × 2 binned, so every figure is per output pixel: a 2.44 µm pitch [1], [2], not the 1.22 µm photodiode.

Uncertainties are an s.d. over repeated captures, a leave-one-view-out jackknife standard error, a fit's 1σ, or a bound stated with its argument.

II. Measured Datasheet¶

Table II summarizes the main camera's results; Sections III to VII give the method behind each one. Three of them can be compared with the manufacturer: the pixel pitch, the focal length and the noise model (Section V-C).

Pixel pitch. Apple's binned pitch is 2.44 µm [1]. The EXIF crop-factor route gives 2.422 ± 0.051 µm (−0.7%; bound from the rounding of the 24 mm equivalent), and the calibration route gives 2.331 ± 0.004 µm (−4.5%).

Focal length. The calibrated value, 7.03 ± 0.15 mm, is 3.9% above the EXIF 6.765 mm. Most of the gap is likely focus breathing: the board was 234 to 365 mm away, and focusing a 6.765 mm thin lens that close moves it 1.9% to 3.0% further from the sensor.

III. Geometry: Intrinsics and Distortion¶

A. Calibration¶

I calibrated with cv2.calibrateCamera [3], [4] on 25 views of a 9 × 6 board with 20.0 mm squares, eight of them with the board near the frame edges and corners. Four distortion coefficients give 1.44 px RMS reprojection error; adding k3 gives 0.86 ± 0.03 px, so I adopt five (Table II). With four, the principal point moves by about 5 px and its jackknife error triples.

B. Uncertainty¶

The fit's own 1σ understates the uncertainty 3–6× (principal point ±1.3 px against ±4.3 px from the jackknife), because corner errors within a view are correlated, so I report the jackknife. A homography fit to each view's undistorted corners, with that view left out of the calibration, leaves 0.67 ± 0.04 px median (bootstrap): the board is flat to about 0.2 mm. The tangential terms are within 2σ of zero, the principal point sits 10.6 px right of and 1.5 px above the frame center, and the board's corners reach 78% of the way to the frame corner.

C. Undistortion¶

On the board row furthest from the principal point, undistortion reduces the maximum deviation from a straight line from 1.35 to 0.69 px (Fig. 1); over all 150 rows, the median falls from 1.36 to 0.52 px.

IV. Spatial Resolution¶

A. Method¶

I measured the MTF with the slanted-edge method [5] on one black-subtracted green plane of the Bayer mosaic, so no demosaicing interpolation enters the edge. A green-plane pixel spans 2p = 4.84 µm. All MTF values are in cycles per green-plane pixel, where Nyquist is 0.5; halve them for full-mosaic pixels. On a synthetic Gaussian edge with a known answer (σ = 1 px), the code's MTF50 was within −0.12%.

For the frame-corner session, the square finder thresholds against the local paper brightness, since one global threshold failed under its uneven light; on the 24 Homework 2 squares it matches the original finder's MTF50 to within 0.0022.

B. Center¶

Against a diffraction (f/1.78, 550 nm) × pixel-aperture prediction, the camera keeps about half the predicted contrast at Nyquist: 0.404 ± 0.032 against 0.785 (Fig. 2). Lens aberrations are the leading suspect, since MTF also falls off axis (Section IV-C).

The center MTF50 varies more between sessions than within one (0.403, 0.327 and 0.453 for Homework 2, the ring-light session and the final one; frame-to-frame s.d. ≤ 0.032), most likely through focus, so I quote the final session's 0.453 with the s.d. of the three sessions, ±0.064, and scale the corner uncertainties by the same fraction. The ring-light session failed at the corners, not the center, so it stays in (without it, ±0.035).

C. Field Dependence¶

For the frame corners, the target's outer squares sat 82% to 84% of the way to each corner, five frames per position at a fixed exposure (Fig. 3). MTF50 there is 0.395 (bottom-left), 0.374 (top-left), 0.344 (bottom-right) and 0.301 (top-right), with frame-to-frame s.d. of 0.003 to 0.010. The corner mean, 0.353 ± 0.050, is 78% of the center; the worst is top-right at 0.301 ± 0.042 (positions as framed in the app). Relative to Nyquist (0.5), the center sits at 0.91 and the corners at 0.60 to 0.79.

MTF50 dips to 0.24–0.29 halfway out and recovers toward the corners, which fits a curved surface of best focus. Refocusing at each position would have made the target's large central square the sharpest; it is among the softest.

Fig. 2. Homework 2 center MTF (± 1 s.d., 6 captures) against the diffraction × pixel-aperture prediction; dashed line: green-plane Nyquist. Frequency is in cycles/µm; multiply by 4.84 µm for cycles per green-plane pixel.
Fig. 3. MTF50 of every square against its distance from the frame center (filled: final session, ± s.d. over 5 frames; open: Homework 2). Labels mark the outermost square at each corner.

V. Noise: The Poisson–Gaussian Model¶

A. Photon Transfer¶

The flat fields were 10 pairs from 0.9% to 96% of saturation at ISO 50 (window light through 2 to 10 sheets of paper), measured on a central 128 × 128 patch of one green plane, away from the lens shading. For each pair, the mean is the average of the two frames above black and the variance is ½Var(A − B). I fit Var = Kμ + K²σr² [6], [7], weighted by 1/variance, through the 9 pairs below 70% of saturation, after removing 1/12 DN² of quantization variance from the intercept. A single frame's variance also holds fixed-pattern PRNU, growing as (pμ)²: fitting single frames gave K 14.3% higher (0.281 DN/e⁻, p = 0.61%). The pair difference cancels it.

B. Results¶

K = 0.246 ± 0.021 DN/e⁻, combining the fit's ±0.014 with a ±0.015 systematic: K is 0.218, 0.229 and 0.246 for fits up to 15%, 30% and 70% of saturation. The intercept constrains the read noise poorly (4.2 ± 2.9 e⁻); 11 dark-frame pairs give 1.694 ± 0.002 DN, or 6.9 ± 0.6 e⁻. The regimes meet at μ = σr² = 47 ± 8 e⁻; the darkest pair (135 e⁻) is 2.9× above that knee, so the data show the start of the bend but not the read-noise regime itself (Fig. 4).

C. Vendor NoiseProfile¶

The DNG's NoiseProfile [8] (S = 8.858 × 10⁻⁵, O = 9.874 × 10⁻⁷), scaled by 3567 DN, gives K = 0.316 DN/e⁻ and σr = 3.54 DN (11.2 e⁻). My gain is 22% lower and my read noise 52% lower in DN. The profile matches my measured variance at 54% of saturation but overstates it toward black, by 2.3× at the darkest pair.

D. Dark Current¶

The 23 lens-capped frames (1/30 to 1 s) give no measurement: the Bayer channels disagree beyond their errors, and the dark level jumps between frames by as much as the whole trend. The one-sided 95% bound is < 0.6 e⁻/s, under 1.3% of the read-noise variance at 1 s.

Fig. 4. Photon transfer curve from the central green-plane patch on linear and logarithmic axes (left), and measured SNR against the model (right). Knees: 47 e⁻ with the dark-frame read noise (adopted), 17.5 e⁻ with the PTC-intercept read noise.

VI. Dynamic Range¶

DR = log₂(3567 DN / 1.694 DN) = 11.04 ± 0.06 stops: white minus black level, over the signal equal to the read noise (SNR = 1 from read noise alone), a ratio that in DN does not depend on the gain.

The ± is a bound. The green sites begin to saturate near 3950 DN rather than 4095 DN, and that ceiling would give 10.98 stops. The headline and the full well keep the declared level, with this as the bound; the color measurement uses 3940 DN, because there it decides which patches count as clipped. For comparison, the EMVA 1288 criterion [7] (SNR = 1 including shot noise) gives 10.9 stops, and SNR = 10 gives 6.7 stops.

VII. Color Accuracy¶

A. Method¶

Three ColorChecker Classic Mini charts were shot under an LED lamp (ISO 400, no patch clipped), normalized to the measured 3940 DN saturation level, reduced to quarter-resolution RGB without demosaicing, shading-corrected per channel, and averaged over the middle half of each patch. The white sheet served only as the flat field; white balance came from patch 22 (neutral 5), the brightest neutral unclipped in every round. A 3 × 3 matrix to XYZ was then fitted by least squares over all 24 patches. Errors are CIEDE2000 [9] against colour-science's ColorChecker24 – After November 2014 set [10], chosen because X-Rite reformulated the chart in November 2014.

B. Results¶

Mean ΔE00 is 12.35 ± 0.08 before the matrix and 3.06 ± 0.04 after; the worst patch falls from 23.20 ± 0.47 to 8.89 ± 0.26, patch 15 (red) (Fig. 5). Uncertainties are the s.d. over three charts, which agree to about 1%. The residual remains because the sensor fails the Luther condition. Carried unchanged to other lights, chart A's matrix (3.11 under the LED) gives 5.79 under a blackbody lamp and 6.94 under daylight (one chart each; about ±0.1 by the chart-to-chart spread).

Fig. 5. CIEDE2000 error per patch before and after the fitted matrix (LED, chart A).

VIII. Beyond the Specification: The Ultra-Wide¶

A. Calibration¶

The same code calibrated the 0.5× ultra-wide (2.22 mm, f/2.2, RGGB) from 33 views, reaching 83% of the way to the frame corner (main camera: 78%). I adopt the rational model (Table III); its radial coefficients trade off against each other (jackknife errors up to 30%), but the curve they define is stable. The focal length, 1620.4 ± 1.9 px, gives 2.21 ± 0.08 mm with the EXIF-route pitch of 1.362 µm, within 0.6% of the EXIF 2.22 mm.

B. Distortion¶

Instead of the expected visible barrel, the raw distortion is small over most of the frame: −0.56 ± 0.04% halfway out and −1.52 ± 0.07% at 83% of the corner radius (Fig. 6a; jackknife), similar in size to the main camera's +1.64 ± 0.09% halfway out. Most of it lies beyond the board's reach.

C. Metal Ruler¶

A metal ruler along the bottom of the frame tests each calibration on a line it never saw. Raw, its edge deviates from a straight line by 32.6 px on the ultra-wide, bending sharply over the last ~500 px at each end (Fig. 6b), and by 16.0 px on the main camera. Within each calibration's coverage, correction reduces this from 19.0 to 7.8 px (ultra-wide) and 13.7 to 6.3 px (main). Over the whole ruler, where the models extrapolate, the main camera only reaches 14.7 px; on the ultra-wide the rational model gives 13.9 px and five coefficients 28.6 px. That chose the model, so for it the ruler is a selection test, not a blind one. All are single frames, ±1.5 px from edge noise (0.2–0.4 px rms). About 6–8 px of bow remains, unexplained.

D. Apple's Own Correction¶

The ultra-wide DNG stores Apple's distortion correction as a WarpRectilinear2 opcode [8] (the main camera's has none), with coefficients that vary slightly per file. Applied raw-to-corrected, it agrees with my rational model to within 6.0 px in every file (0.87 px median RMS) after one free scale factor, within 0.2% of 1; without it, 5.6 px in the median file and 9.6 px in the worst. It straightens the ruler to 13.0 px; the other direction bends it to 51 px.

Decisions and Verification Statement¶

What I decided, and what I rejected.

  • Five distortion coefficients for the main camera, the rational model for the ultra-wide. Four coefficients gave 1.44 px RMS on the main camera; five gave 0.86. On the ultra-wide the metal ruler decided: the rational model straightens it to 13.9 px, five coefficients only to 28.6.
  • The EXIF-route pixel pitch (2.42 µm), not the calibration route (2.33 µm). The calibration's focal length is inflated by close focus.
  • MTF on one green plane of the raw mosaic, never on demosaiced data.
  • MTF uncertainty from the spread between sessions (±0.064), not within the final session (±0.005). Focus moved the center value more than anything else.
  • Read noise from dark-frame pairs, not the PTC intercept, which carries ±69% uncertainty.
  • Dark current as an upper bound, not the 0.33 e⁻/s fit.
  • For color, saturation at 3940 DN, not the declared 4095, because the green sites pile up from about 3950 DN. That excluded seven blackbody patches.

AI use. I used Claude (Anthropic) to write most of the analysis code, to diagnose problems in my captures, to explain concepts and to draft written answers, which I reviewed and edited. Claude also assembled this report and results.json, drafted this statement for me to review and edit, wrote the README and the pytest suite, checked each new capture session as I shot it, and wrote project1_checks.py: the jackknife uncertainties, the frame-corner MTF, the ultra-wide calibration, the metal-ruler test and the reading of Apple's opcode.

How I checked the results.

  • Known answers before real data. The slanted-edge code recovered a synthetic σ = 1 px edge's MTF50 to −0.12%. The PTC code recovered the lecture 5 simulator's K to −0.04% ± 0.21% and σr to +0.30% ± 0.70% over 20 runs. The new square finder matches the old one's MTF50 on all 24 Homework 2 squares to within 0.0022.
  • Automated tests. 38 pytest tests in tests/ run the MTF, photon-transfer, color, opcode, square-finder and straightness code on synthetic inputs with known answers.
  • Tests the calibrations were not fitted to. The metal ruler (Section VIII-C), though it also chose the ultra-wide model; Apple's correction is the independent check, agreeing with my model to 6 px after one overall scale (9.6 px without it).
  • Cross-checks. Pixel pitch two ways against Apple's 2.44 µm; read noise from the fit and the dark frames (1.3σ apart); single-frame against pair gain (+14.3%, matching the simulator's +14.2% for a known PRNU); color across three charts (3.03 to 3.11).

Failure modes I found.

  • My first read-noise fit on the simulator was +5.2% (8σ) high. Rounding adds 1/12 DN² to every variance; subtracting it removed the bias.
  • A flatness test that mixed two effects. Homework 2's homography test left 2.22 px, and I blamed the board. On undistorted corners, with each view left out of its own calibration, it is 0.67 px, and 86% of the raw residual was radial: lens distortion. The board is flat to about 0.2 mm.
  • The calibration's own 1σ was 3–6× too small against the jackknife (principal point ±1.3 px against ±4.3 px).
  • The first frame-corner session failed. Shot through a ring light, it reached only 66–69% of the way to the corners, and the homework's square finder found one or two of five squares per frame because of the light's hot spot. I re-shot without the ring light (82–84%) and replaced the finder.
  • I first applied Apple's correction backwards. It then disagreed with my model by up to 31 px and bent the ruler to 51 px; the ruler showed the right direction (13 px). Its coefficients also differ per file, and using another file's changed the result by 2 px.

What I am still unsure about.

  • Whether focus stayed locked across the frame-corner positions; the DNG does not record it.
  • The 6–8 px bow left on the metal ruler after correction, on both cameras.
  • Which direction the DNG specification intends for the warp; I used the one the ruler supports.
  • Variance/mean rises with signal (0.22 to 0.32): sensor non-linearity or raw-path processing, so the gain carries ±0.015 DN/e⁻.
  • The vendor NoiseProfile's read noise is 2× mine in DN (1.6× in electrons), and I do not know how Apple derives it.
  • The checkerboard square size (20 ± 0.5 mm by ruler, while the slanted-edge sheet printed at 95.8%). It scales the board distances by up to 4%, but not f_px or the distortion.
  • The focus-breathing account of the 3.9 ± 2.1% focal-length gap is a thin-lens estimate: consistent, not proven.
  • The color charts' production date, against the post-2014 reference set.
